correctness.rationale: The admissible set is exhaustively partitioned by triples of the eight unit-sphere edges. Exact elimination over \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2)\) gives 48 feasible one-parameter families. On each family each shifted norm is the maximum of eight affine functions and is therefore convex, so its maximum is at an interval endpoint. The exact checker also evaluates all support-change points, 128 checks total, and proves both shifted norms are at most \(2\sqrt2-1\). The explicit admissible pair x=(1,sqrt(2)-1), y=(3-2sqrt(2),1) attains both bounds, so raising to any \(p\ge1\) and adding gives the stated formula. The checker was run from the packaged source before acceptance.

value.rationale: The exponent-p family is explicitly introduced as a generalized geometric invariant in the defining paper, so determining its full regular-octagon profile is a natural exact problem. The result is not obtained by substituting p into the known \(p=2\) value: it requires the stronger and independently proved coordinatewise cap on both shifted norms. That cap explains why one equilateral configuration is extremal for every \(p\ge1\) and provides a reusable structural description of the octagonal equilateral geometry.
